  Let me now define:

  ```ts
  export interface BusyForInfo {
    member: Member   // the agent using the lane
    run: Run
  }

  const BUSY_STATES = new Set<RunState>(["queued", "running", "verifying", "waiting_approval"])

  export function laneBorrower(member: Member, runs: Run[], members: Member[]): Member | null {
    if (member.kind !== "agent") return null
    if (identityOf(member).role !== null) return null // only raw CLIs
    const laneIds = new Set(member.agent?.lanes ?? [])
    if (laneIds.size === 0) return null
    const borrowers = runs.filter((run) => laneIds.has(run.lane_id) && run.agent_id !== member.id && BUSY_STATES.has(run.state))
    if (borrowers.length === 0) return null
    const run = pickLatestRun(borrowers)
    return members.find((m) => m.id === run.agent_id) ?? null
  }
  ```

  pickLatestRun is private in state.ts; reuse it there. For sidebar import, we export laneBorrower from office/state.ts.

I'll include queued, running, verifying — those mean lane busy/incoming. Waiting approval: the lane isn't running the process... probably freed. Hmm, actually does faztudo free the lane while waiting for approval? Lane `running` count — decrement on completion only? Unclear. I'll include queued/running/verifying (the ones where work is happening or imminent). Actually including waiting_approval also seems reasonable for "this lane is tied up".
